facilities.notes: China Daily (5 Jun 2026) puts China Mobile's whole Zhongwei campus, parks A and B, at 332MW IT in production across 12 buildings. Park B is 202MW of that. Park A's share is not published, so live MW stays blank. Signed AI computing scale of 635MW in 2025 is a contracted figure, not built capacity. The city's draft development plan (Dec 2025) gives four China Mobile parks, A to D, at 1.5GW IT and 596,000 standard racks at full build. That is a plan figure for the whole campus and is not recorded as planned MW. [2026-10-19] Science and Technology Daily (May 2025) says about 48,000 racks are in service across seven buildings with occupancy above 99.8%, which matches this row's live racks. That first phase cost 4 billion yuan on about 200 mu at the edge of the Tengger Desert. Phase 2 was planned at 6.7 billion yuan and over 80,000 standard racks by end 2025. The phase 2 figures may sit in other parks of the campus, so they are not added to this row. [2026-10-20] Xinhua (18 May 2026) says the China Mobile Zhongwei hub has delivered 81,000 standard racks with over 60,000 PFLOPS schedulable. This is a campus figure across parks, not Park A alone, so live racks for this row are unchanged. [2026-10-23] Planning notices for phases 3 (Dec 2023), 4 (Aug 2024) and 5 (Apr 2025) all sit on the same 129,383 sqm plot (about 194 mu). Phase 4 adds machine buildings 2-2 (18,183.15 sqm) and 5 (21,785.37 sqm). The phase 5 notice puts total floor area on the plot at 172,198.29 sqm. These are linked to Park A by plot size.

water_cooling.cooling_note: Building A01 ran a water-cooling trial in 2018; building A05 then used air cooling. Later Park B uses a dual-source glycol/refrigerant system.
water_cooling.note: Building-level history, not a campus-wide design.

aliases: 中国移动（宁夏中卫）数据中心B园区
facilities.notes: Put into full use on 30 May 2026 with 202MW IT in production (China Daily, 5 Jun 2026). Billed as the first large park integrating generation, grid, load and storage, with green power above 80% and an all-in power cost held at 0.36 yuan/kWh. 宁夏日报 (13 Apr 2026) describes a Park B project of 6.149bn yuan with 6 data halls, 245.2MW of load and about 13,624 physical racks, still at the excavation stage. That does not match the 202MW in full use on 30 May 2026. The two may be different builds within Park B. The 245.2MW basis is not stated and is not recorded as planned MW. [2026-10-13] Phase 2 permits: B07 reissued 21 Aug 2026 at 167,359 sqm, B13 issued 3 Apr 2026 and reissued 30 Jun 2026 at 36,688 sqm. No IT MW for phase 2, so planned MW is unchanged. Science and Technology Daily (9 Jul 2026) reports the Park B ultra-large computing centre in operation, with a wind and liquid dual cold-source system in building B13. Phase 2 permits continue, so the row stays operational without a phase split. [2026-10-19] The Park B B01 and B02 machine building EPC contract with the CSCEC Third Bureau, Huaxin and Xiangjiang consortium is 1,631.86 million yuan including tax. Equipment is 900.63 million yuan of that. The planned site start was 15 May 2025 and planned completion 30 Jul 2025. [2026-10-20] Science and Technology Daily (May 2025) says China Mobile Ningxia's Zhongwei phase 1 has 7 server buildings and 48,000 racks in service. Phase 2 was due to add over 80,000 standard racks by end 2025. The long-term plan is 150,000 standard racks. The article does not name Park B, so no rack figure is set on this row. [2026-10-21] Approval and power context: Datang Zhongwei New Energy's June 2026 EIA covers expanding its 330kV Chijing substation (驰景变电站) from 2 to 4 x 250MVA. The station is the grid part of a source-grid-load-storage project made up of 500MW of PV (already grid-connected), 50MW/100MWh of storage, two 110kV switching stations and 498.5MW of load. Its stated purpose is dual supply for data centre companies. The EIA does not name China Mobile. The link to Park B rests on the Park B No.2 substation EIA, which connects to those two switching stations. [2026-10-21] Approval: Park B phase 2 sits on 14.209 ha (213.14 mu) west of Park B phase 1. The March 2026 scheme had seven data centre buildings and a 110kV substation, with 193,385.9 sqm of floor area. A pre-approval notice for a local adjustment ran 11 to 19 Aug 2026. It merges the six planned buildings B07 to B12 into one B07 data centre of 167,359.35 sqm and drops the F07 to F12 process water pump houses and water treatment station. It adds a 948.26 sqm warehouse and raises the diesel platforms from 4 to 7. Total floor area becomes 206,139.68 sqm.

power_supply.renewable_note: Xinhua says the China Mobile Zhongwei data centre has a direct green power connection. The supplier is not named in this article.
power_supply.note: Direct green power supply reported without a named generator. The Datang Zhongwei cloud base green supply project is the likely source but that link is left in unassigned.
power_supply.basis: Article names China Mobile Zhongwei data centre and its direct green power connection.

facilities.notes: 310MW IT at full build-out (人民邮电报 2025-04-08 and 证券时报 2025-03-25 both say IT load). SASAC (13 May 2026) calls the same figure installed capacity. In April 2025 four buildings were operating, four under construction and over ten planned. Live MW is not published. The city's draft development plan (17 Dec 2025) gives the campus as 350 mu, 8bn yuan, 10 halls and 18,000 racks. That conflicts with the 120,000 standard racks on this row from Unicom. The plan may count physical high-density racks. The row keeps Unicom's figure. [2026-10-14] The DC8 liquid-cooling build was tendered in 2026 with 48 liquid-cooled PODs of 500kW each, about RMB 375m across EPC lots (通信产业网, 14 Jul 2026). POD ratings are not summed into IT load. Park 2's new build is on the Ningxia 2026 key construction list. [2026-10-18] A Zhongwei natural resources bureau notice (Sep 2026) gives the Park 1 main campus site as 133,398 sqm (200.1 mu) in Zhongwei Industrial Park. Grant terms are not stated. (中卫市人民政府 (中卫市自然资源局), 2026-09-17) [2026-10-18] A Sep 2026 plan revision for Park 2 gives its site as 103,282 sqm (154.92 mu) and enlarges the No.9 data centre building to 79,540 sqm of floor area. Park 2 also has a No.3 substation of 3,353 sqm. (中卫市人民政府 (中卫市自然资源局), 2026-08-24) [2026-10-18] Jiemian reports that Manycore Tech (群核科技) draws AI compute support from the Zhongwei cloud data centre. The article does not tie it to a building, so it is not listed as a compute user. (界面新闻, 2026-04-23) [2026-10-19] In Nov 2024 phase 1 covered 200 mu with six planned buildings. Two were in operation with 1,500 racks of 4kW and 2,000 racks of 8kW and over 14,000 GPUs. Phase 2 started in the second half of 2024. Phases 1 and 2 cover 350 mu with ten buildings and over 300MW in total. [2026-10-20] C114's tender tally for H1 2026 says China Unicom's Ningxia Zhongwei cloud data centre liquid-cooled and air-cooled MEP works were tendered in that half. Their combined budget was over 1 billion yuan. Winners are not named. [2026-10-21] Approval: a pre-approval notice for a local optimisation of the Zhongwei cloud data centre scheme ran 17 to 24 Sep 2026. The site in Zhongwei Industrial Park covers 133,398 sqm (200.1 mu). It is bounded by China Mobile land to the east, Fengyun Road to the south and Unicom's Park 2 to the west. Data hall building No.5 grows from 30,337.9 to 33,963.31 sqm, which the notice ties to a process upgrade. The design unit is 中讯邮电咨询设计院有限公司. [2026-10-22] Approval: a building planning permit was issued on 14 Sep 2026 to China Unicom Ningxia for an emergency water pool, two warehouses and diesel generator platform 9 at the Zhongwei cloud data centre. Total floor area is 4,519.59 sqm, of which 2,619.06 sqm is underground. The site is south of Fengyun Road in Zhongwei Industrial Park. [2026-10-22] Approval: a land-use planning permit was issued on 19 Aug 2026 for a new gatehouse and fire access platform at Park 2 of the Zhongwei cloud data centre. The plot is 3,282 sqm (4.92 mu) of industrial land obtained by transfer (出让), approved under 卫政土批字〔2026〕12号. [2026-10-23] Approval: the works planning permit for substation No. 2 (6405022026GG0007627) was issued on 11 Feb 2026. It covers 2,894.51 sqm of floor area, with 2,055.49 sqm above ground and 839.02 sqm below.

facilities.notes: Building 1 (75MW IT) is being built and due in H2 2026 (人民日报, 28 Jul 2026). 600MW IT is the stage 1 plan (经济日报, 8 Feb 2026). A 330kV supply project serves the site. A reported investment of about 50bn yuan rests on one headline and is not recorded. The December 2024 investment contract covered a two-centre project of 500MW IT in three phases. The second centre is in Xuanhe. The later 600MW first-stage figure for the Cloud Base site is used for this row. People's Daily (28 Jul 2026) repeats that hall 1 is structurally complete and due in the second half of 2026 with 30,000 standard racks. [2026-10-23] The 330kV substation EIA says the Cloud Base park covers 500 mu and plans buildings 1 to 8 with 39,424 cabinets of 16kW and 128 of 4kW. Final maximum load is about 800MW. That is total load, not IT load, so planned MW is unchanged. Near-term operation is planned for June 2027 and final operation for June 2028. This is later than the second half of 2026 given for hall 1 by People's Daily. The developer 宁夏卫联算都 is a wholly owned subsidiary of 中联云港科技股份有限公司. facilities.notes: Phase 1 building A1 topped out on 28 Jul 2025; 经济日报 (23 Apr 2026) lists the base as under accelerated construction. The operator gives 1.2GW IT as the cluster plan with 3,600MVA supply. 新华网宁夏 and 中国新闻网 give 2,050MW as total planned capacity, basis unclear. The lower operator figure is used. Phase 1 targets of 50MW by Sep 2025 and 200MW by end 2025 are not confirmed delivered. Not related to CICC. A company vice president said on 7 Sep 2026 that it is also planning a GW-class park in the Yuding area of Zhongwei. No capacity, investment or site record exists for it, so it is not a row. [2026-10-13] On 30 Apr 2026 part of hall A1 was in operation and running AI workloads while other areas were still being fitted out, so the campus is expanding. Live capacity is not quantified. The base is 836 mu in three phases. Phase 1 is 252 mu with 4 data halls, 4 diesel generator buildings and 2 substations. [2026-10-13] China Gold Data's release of 30 Jul 2025 gives 1.2GW IT as the total for its Zhongwei 'dual cluster', the zero-carbon base plus the Xuanhe green AI base 25km away. The whole 1.2GW sits on this row and the Xuanhe row stays blank so the cluster is counted once. Land permits for phases 1 to 3 total 43,750 cabinets of 16kW, which are not standard racks and are not converted. The 2,000MW figure seen earlier was not found in any permit or EIA this run. [2026-10-19] Zhongwei's environment bureau approved the EIA for the phase 2 and 3 330kV substation in Jan 2026 (卫环函〔2026〕4号). The substation has six 240MVA transformers and a total investment of 391.31 million yuan. [2026-10-20] A Jul 2025 report gives the Zhongwei cluster a planned power supply capacity of 3,600 MVA, with 1.2GW of IT and design PUE below 1.2. Phase 2 is 9 computing centres and 9 power centres of about 245,000 sqm. Phase 3 is about 342,000 sqm, with full completion expected in 2027. Building A1 topped out on 28 Jul 2025. Total investment is about 40 billion yuan. [2026-10-23] Approval: works planning permits for the phase 3 330kV outdoor substation buildings (4,110.79 sqm) were issued on 21 Oct 2025 and reissued on 8 Jun 2026.

facilities.notes: In Wangyuan village, Xuanhe town, separate from Parks A and B in the Western Cloud Base. The plan notice (6 Mar 2026) covers 31.5 ha with 12 data buildings and three 110kV substations. Building permits cover D01 to D04 (19 Mar 2026), D05 and D06 (Jul 2026) and D07 to D10 (Sep 2026). Contractor filings by 城地香江 (603887) give D01 at 34MW IT and D03 at about 65MW IT under China Mobile Zone D. Zone D is matched to the Xuanhe Park by building numbers; no source states the link outright. Planned 99MW is the sum of the two disclosed buildings and is a floor for the park. D03 was due for delivery by 30 Jul 2026; no source confirms it went live. Stage rests on the city government report of the mayor reviewing construction progress in the Xuanhe area on 10 Mar 2026. [2026-10-13] Building permit for machine buildings D07 to D10 issued 20 Sep 2026, 175,738 sqm. C114 reports an MEP EPC tender for D07 to D10 with a CNY 3.298bn budget and no MW. The 99MW floor is unchanged. C114 reports an August 2026 China Mobile tender for Ningxia Zhongwei Data Center Zone D MEP EPC with a CNY 3.54bn budget; buildings and MW are not stated. (C114通信网, 2026-09-03) [2026-10-19] China Mobile posted the candidate list for the Zone D buildings D03 and D04 MEP EPC on 23 Jan 2026. The consortium of CSCEC Third Bureau First Company, Xiangjiang Systems and Shanghai Posts & Telecom Design Institute bid 1,125.85 million yuan including tax. The excluding-tax unit price was 15,047.61 yuan per kW. No MW is stated, so none is derived. [2026-10-19] C114 counts Zone D building MEP EPC tenders in Ningxia at over 4.1 billion yuan in Sep 2026, led by the D07 to D10 package at 3.298 billion yuan. [2026-10-20] C114's Q3 2026 review says China Mobile's tender budgets for its Ningxia Zhongwei site exceeded 8.3 billion yuan in the quarter, led by the Zone D MEP EPC packages. The article does not split the total by building or park. [2026-10-20] The draft detailed plan for the Xuanhe area of the Zhongwei data centre cluster covers 819.54 ha (12,293 mu), of which 573.40 ha (8,601 mu) is construction land, south of Wangyuan village in Xuanhe town. It was published for comment in December 2025. [2026-10-22] The substation EIA says the operator signed the state land use right sale contract 卫地(G)〔2026〕-9号 on 12 Mar 2026 for 31.4976 ha (472.46 mu). This makes the held government land a sale (出让), so tenure is leasehold. [2026-10-22] A result notice for the Xuanhe Zone D No.2 110kV substation EPC was published in Sep 2026 through 公诚管理咨询. Aggregators name different winners, 中国建筑第六工程局 on one and 山东省工业设备安装集团 on another, so no contractor is added until the notice is read. [2026-10-22] The Xuanhe area wastewater treatment and reuse project for the Zhongwei data centre cluster, built by 宁夏水务投资集团, had its EIA approved on 13 May 2026 (卫环函〔2026〕53号). It serves the cluster, not only this campus. [2026-10-23] MW conflict: a July 2026 report on the D01 and D02 MEP EPC framework result says the two buildings have about 71MW of total IT power (2栋楼IT总功率约71MW). The held 99MW floor uses D01 at 34MW plus D03 at about 65MW. If 71MW covers D01 and D02, D01 to D03 would total about 136MW. Estimated value excluding tax was 1,189.99 million yuan. A second lot went to a consortium named as Inspur (浪潮), 机械工业第六设计院 and 山东邮电. The report does not map winners to lots explicitly and gives no full legal names, so that consortium is not added as a contractor. [2026-10-23] Bid evaluation for the Zone D major civil EPC covering machine buildings D09 and D10, outdoor pipelines and roads, a fire water tank and a circulating pump house finished on 11 Aug 2026. Shortlisted bids were 宁夏交通建设股份有限公司 (314.50 million yuan), 宁夏兴启建设有限公司 (316.32 million yuan) and 中国江苏国际经济技术合作集团有限公司 (319.89 million yuan), with a 289 day build period. These are candidates, not an award. [2026-10-24] 城地香江 said on 10 Sep 2026 that the D01 and D02 MEP EPC framework lot 1 contract was signed with China Mobile Ningxia. Signed price is 622.82 million yuan including tax, of which 5.23 million yuan is design. Workload split is CSCEC3 First 33.8%, Xiangjiang Systems 65.35% and Shanghai PTDI 0.85%. MEP crews were due on site from 9 Aug 2026, with handover targeted by 30 Dec 2026 (153 days). The framework runs to 31 Dec 2027. [2026-10-24] Approvals: a works planning permit for the Xuanhe park maintenance support building (O&M support centre, 13,000 sqm) was issued on 8 Jun 2026.

facilities.notes: Zhonglian Data Group's second Zhongwei site, in Xuanhe town east of the 三党公路. The December 2024 investment contract covered two centres of 500MW IT in total, and the Cloud Base row carries the later 600MW first-stage figure for that site alone, so no MW is recorded here. Land-use permit for 169,536 sqm issued 1 Jul 2025 and a building permit for buildings 1 to 4 and a 330kV substation on 2 Jul 2025. A city report places the Xuanhe area under construction in March 2026 but does not name this project, so the stage stays at land and permitting. The Ningxia 2026 key project list includes the project. [2026-10-19] The article says 在中卫宣和片区，中联数据绿色智算产业基地建设正酣。一期规划的1栋数据中心与1栋动力中心已封顶，设计IT容量100兆瓦、标准机架4万架. So phase 1 had one data centre and one power centre topped out by December 2025. The 100MW is a stated design IT load, but it may be the whole base, so planned MW is left for review. The tie to this row rests on Zhonglian Data plus the Xuanhe location. [2026-10-19] People's Daily quotes Zhonglian Data Group's northwest regional manager on site. Phase 1 data hall No. 1 is under construction and due in use in the second half of 2026, able to hold 30,000 standard racks. The article does not name Xuanhe. [2026-10-20] Stage date is the first dated report of works. The EIA says the Xuanhe computing park has formally started construction, with hoarding up and site servicing and levelling done, and an 11,000 sqm construction camp built. It does not give the start day. [2026-10-20] EIA background: the park covers 500 mu in two phases with data centre buildings 1 to 8 and an office. It plans 39,424 cabinets of 16kW and 128 of 4kW. Final maximum load is about 800MW. That is a grid load figure, not stated IT load, so planned MW stays blank. Near-term operation is planned for June 2027 and full operation for June 2028. [2026-10-20] The developer 宁夏西部智算大数据科技有限公司 was set up in January 2025 with 10 million yuan of registered capital. The EIA calls it a subsidiary of 中联云港科技股份有限公司. A CSCEC Third Bureau (中建三局) project office sits east of the park. The EIA does not say it is this park's contractor. [2026-10-21] The water EIA says Zhonglian signed with Zhongwei in early January 2025 for a two-site computing base of about 1,000 mu: about 500 mu in the main zone and about 500 mu in Xuanhe, with total investment of about 50 billion yuan across both sites. [2026-10-21] Approval: Zhongwei Natural Resources Bureau posted a pre-approval notice for a local optimisation and adjustment of the Zone A planning and design scheme on 2026-09-17. [2026-10-22] Approval: Zhongwei Ecology and Environment Bureau approved the EIA for the Zone A 330kV substation of 宁夏西部智算大数据科技有限公司 on 30 Jun 2026, under 卫环函〔2026〕75号.

facilities.notes: Guangdong Haoyun Changsheng Network builds this campus through its project company 中卫浩远科技 in Zhongwei Industrial Park, Shapotou District. The plan is five data centre buildings in three phases, about 115,536 sqm, RMB 3.36bn on 200 mu. Phase 1 started in July 2024 and phase 2 in Q4 2024; the stage date is the first dated report of works under way. The structure topped out on 29 Oct 2025. The company targeted operation by end 2025 but no go-live is reported. It is item 82(6) on the Ningxia 2026 key construction list. No IT load figure exists, so MW is blank. People's Daily (28 Jul 2026) lists Haoyun among eight ultra-large AI projects signed in Zhongwei and the company markets a gigawatt-scale Zhongwei site; that may be a newer signing and is not on this row. [2026-10-19] Haoyun Changsheng held a topping out ceremony on 29 Oct 2025 for buildings 3 and 4 of its 宁夏中卫大型智算产业集群, about 100 days after structural work began. The design uses a 风液同源 air and liquid cooling architecture, and the company is working on 100kW per rack solutions. The article says Haoyun has three projects in Zhongwei, so it is not certain this cluster is the same site as this row. [2026-10-20] Approval: planning permit issued 25 Jul 2024 to 中卫浩远科技有限公司 for data centre No. 2 (23,680.91 sqm), complex building No. 6, a gatehouse, generator yards 2 and 3 and fuel tanks. Total 27,051.35 sqm. The site is in Zhongwei Industrial Park, west to 卫云路 and north to 凤云路. [2026-10-20] Approval: planning permit issued 17 Feb 2025 to 中卫浩远科技有限公司 for data centre No. 4 (23,680.91 sqm), generator yards 6 and 7 and fuel tank 6, on the same Zhongwei Industrial Park site. The October 2025 topping out of buildings 3 and 4 likely refers to this site. [2026-10-21] A State Grid EIA (Zhongwei ecology bureau, 4 Sep 2026) lists existing 110kV lines named 凤浩远Ⅰ线 and 雅浩远Ⅰ线 from the Fengyun and Yayun switching stations. The names point to two 110kV feeds into the held Haoyuan substation. Inferred from line names. [2026-10-22] Approval: a building planning permit was issued on 5 Mar 2026 to 中卫浩远科技有限公司 for an above-ground water tank and pump house (No. 11) at the Haoyun Changsheng Ningxia data centre. Floor area is 2,337.56 sqm. The site lies west of 卫云路 and south of 凤云路 in Zhongwei Industrial Park. [2026-10-22] Approval: a building planning permit was issued on 18 Mar 2024 to 中卫浩远科技有限公司 for the No. 7 110kV substation building and support facilities, 2,018 sqm of floor area, west of 经十五路 and south of 凤云路. This is the building for the 126MVA substation already held. [2026-10-24] Approval: a building planning permit (6405022026GG0008680) was issued on 5 Mar 2026 to 中卫浩远科技有限公司 for the No. 3 data centre building and No. 3 generator platform, 26,098.83 sqm of floor area. The site is bounded by 卫云路 to the west and 凤云路 to the north, with land of 中能建绿色数字科技（中卫）有限公司 to the south. [2026-10-24] Approval: a building planning permit (6405022026GG0009677) was issued on 5 Mar 2026 to 中卫浩远科技有限公司 for the No. 4 data centre building and No. 6 generator platform, 26,020.83 sqm of floor area, on the same site as the No. 3 building.

facilities.notes: NHC Innovation, the digital arm of the National Housing Company, announced at LEAP 2026 a SAR 3.3bn data centre in Khuzam Digital Valley, Riyadh, the zone it launched in January 2026. Phase 1 is 15MW, due by mid-2027, rising to 65MW over six to eight years. The source calls this capacity and gives no IT load basis. The sponsor says construction has started but gives no date, and only a secondary outlet reports it, so the stage is held at announced. Edaily (2 Sep 2026) quotes Naver Cloud saying nothing has been decided on its own Saudi data centre. Coordinates are Riyadh city. [2026-10-19] Okaz reports Khuzam Digital Valley was launched on 26 Jan 2026 as a data centre and digital technology city of about 200,000 sqm inside the Khuzam destination, led by NHC Innovation. The area is for the whole digital city, not the 65MW data centre plot, so no land op is proposed. No contractor, power or cooling detail is published. [2026-10-19] MENA Startup Digest gives phase 1 as 15MW due mid next year, growing to 65MW over six to eight years. The MW basis is not stated. [2026-10-20] Asharq Al-Awsat (9 Sep 2026) describes the 65MW as a target IT load of up to 65MW by 2033, for SAR 3.3 billion. MCIT's LEAP 2026 release gives 65MW by 2033 without a basis. Supports IT load as the basis, from press only. No contractor, power or cooling named. [2026-10-21] MENA Startup Digest (6 Sep 2026) says NHC Innovation 'has started construction of Khuzam Digital Valley' but gives no start date, so no stage history entry is proposed. Asharq Al-Awsat (9 Sep 2026) does not mention construction. A MEED item of 24 Nov 2025 on an infrastructure contract at the Khuzam housing development does not mention the data centre, so no contractor is linked.

China Mobile Hohhot Intelligent Computing Center
facilities.notes: The campus covers about 1,000 mu in the Horinger New Area. The two 2016 profiles give different investment totals, 22 billion yuan and about 15 billion yuan, so the 22 billion yuan figure is a campus plan and is not build cost. Total compute is 20,100P, of which 16,700P is intelligent compute. The campus used 850 million kWh in 2025. A trade press headline dated 2026-10-12 reports a 20,100P expansion completed at the Hohhot intelligent computing centre. [2026-10-15] Inner Mongolia Daily (via IT Home, 2026-10-12) says buildings B25 and B27 are complete with 120MW of IT load. China Construction Third Bureau built them for about 2.7 billion yuan. Planned MW shows this 120MW as a floor for the campus. Liquid cold-plate cooling, campus PUE 1.15 and 88% green power are stated in the same piece. A token factory built with Volcano Engine landed at the China Mobile intelligent computing centre in the Horinger New Area in mid August 2026. [2026-10-18] The site hosts about 20,000 AI accelerator cards and is described as China Mobile's largest single liquid-cooled intelligent computing centre. Expansion is planned. (新华网, 2026-06-22) [2026-10-19] C114 reports that China Mobile tendered MEP works for machine room buildings B17 and B18 in Hohhot in Sep 2026, worth over 2 billion yuan in total. [2026-10-19] Xinhua says the centre covers about 1,000 mu and has over 2,390 AI servers deployed, with domestic chips above 89 percent. [2026-10-20] The B15 contract filing says lots 1 to 4 cover machine buildings B13, B14, B15 and B16. Each building has an IT capacity ceiling of 35MW, so the four total 140MW. This is a separate build from the 120MW held for B25 and B27. Planned MW is not changed here. [2026-10-20] C114's H1 2026 tender tally puts the Hohhot DC B11 to B16 machine building MEP works at 3.037 billion yuan. [2026-10-21] Approval: the civil works project for machine buildings B17 and B18 (中国移动呼和浩特数据中心B17-B18机房楼土建工程) was filed on 4 Jun 2026. It has 650 million yuan of investment, about 82,000 sqm of floor area at 6.9m storey height, and a planned build from June 2026 to December 2027. This is separate from the B17/B18 MEP tenders held on the row. [2026-10-22] Approval: Inner Mongolia ecology department published its EIA approval for the new 220kV substation No. 3 on 20 Jul 2026. The EIA describes the whole China Mobile (Hohhot) data centre project as 12 billion yuan of investment on 1,486.5 mu, with 18 data halls, two spare parts stores, a training centre and six monitoring centres. Phase 1 is in operation and phases 2 to 4 are under construction. The 1,486.5 mu (about 991,000 sqm) differs from the 1,000 mu held.

facilities.notes: The park covers 100 hectares in the Shengle cluster, about 25 km south of Hohhot. The 100,000 rack figure is a 2014 campus plan, and current built racks are not published. China Telecom plans more than 10 billion yuan of computing investment across Inner Mongolia during the 15th Five-Year Plan, including a Horinger and Ulanqab dual park described as gigawatt-scale. That plan has no figures per site and is kept here only as context. No IT load figure is published. China Telecom Inner Mongolia says that of nearly 7 billion yuan invested in the region since the 14th Five-Year Plan, about 2.3 billion went to the Cloud Computing Inner Mongolia Information Park. (新华财经（中国金融信息网）, 2026-08-22) [2026-10-18] The D9 and D10 computing centres phase 1 electromechanical EPC had a budget of 1.229 billion yuan including tax and an IT capacity of 70MW. It was split into two lots, each won by a consortium of China Comservice units. The 70MW covers D9 and D10 phase 1 only, so planned MW for the park stays blank. (通信产业报 (网易号), 2026-07-14) [2026-10-19] China Telecom tendered the electromechanical EPC for the B12 intelligent computing centre and B16 power centre at the park in Jul 2026 with a budget of 754 million yuan. No winner was found. [2026-10-19] In Aug 2026 China Telecom issued further tenders for the Inner Mongolia information park with combined budgets above 300 million yuan. Packages were not itemised. [2026-10-21] The B12 and B16 M&E EPC (budget 754 million yuan when tendered in Jul 2026) was reported awarded on 12 Sep 2026 for 314 million yuan including tax. B12 is 20.488 MW IT. This covers one building, so park planned MW stays blank. [2026-10-23] The B2 and B4 computing centre EPC award (中通服咨询设计研究院 with 中亿丰建设集团) was for 250,125,712.06 yuan against a planned 250.23 million yuan, with a 386-day duration. The supervision award to 中邮通建设咨询 was 3,718,120 yuan.

华为云和林格尔数据中心
facilities.notes: The 75 billion yuan figure comes from Xinhua Finance with no phase breakdown. Treat it as a campus ceiling until Huawei confirms it. China Daily (2025-06-26) says Huawei resumed full-scale construction in the Horinger New Area, so later phases are likely still being built. No MW figure is published. This campus is separate from Huawei Cloud Ulanqab. A Horinger New Area notice dated 2026-09-23 records completion acceptance of the second batch of works in Yungu West Zone phase 1. [2026-10-17] Xinhua Finance reports that Huawei invested 75bn yuan to build the Huawei Cloud Horinger data centre. The source gives no breakdown or MW. (Xinhua Finance (新华财经), 2026-08-12) [2026-10-19] Sina Finance (2026-03-24) gives the Yungu South phase 1 site as 155,094 sqm. The land counterparty is not named. [2026-10-19] Horinger New Area government posted on 2026-09-23 that the Yungu West zone phase 1 second batch completed its completion acceptance filing (竣工验收备案). Sina (2025-07-14) says the site opened on 2025-07-12 with capacity for over 3 million servers. [2026-10-22] Phase 1 south zone data centre building 3 has topped out, per a Horinger New Area post dated 2026-10-09. It is Huawei's first 3D data centre in north China. The design stacks cooling, IT, power and backup power on separate floors. It will host Ascend 950 chips on Huawei's 1024 supernode design. facilities.notes: The campus is in the north of the Bayin core area on 574 mu. Phase 1 is partly operating. The rest of phase 1 and phase 2 were under construction in August 2026, with full operation targeted for 2027. The 300 MW figure that circulates is the wind and solar plant that feeds the campus by a 220 kV private line, grid-connected in July 2025. It is not data centre load. The storage is 45 MW. The operator is China Financial Data Group (中金数据). It is not CICC the investment bank. Ten of 12 planned buildings are built and in use; the last two are due by end 2026 (Xinhua Daily Telegraph, 2026-10-12). [2026-10-16] The builder's official account (BUCG Development, 2026-09-24) gives the cluster a total IT capacity of 800MW across over 1,100 mu. Zone ABC is about 25,000 racks in use since July 2025, and Zone D (530 mu) began in March 2025 and is near completion. The 800MW is held as a note because the operator has not stated it. [2026-10-17] Phase 1 is partly operating. Phases 1 and 2 are still finishing structure and electrical works, with full operation expected in 2027. (投资界 (pedaily), 2026-08-17) [2026-10-20] The Economic Observer (16 Aug 2026) says the 300 MW wind, solar and storage plant sits 18 km from the campus. It supplies about 850 GWh of self-generated green power a year and can replace up to 40 percent of the campus power with renewables. Xinhua (9 Jul 2026) gives the distance as 16 km. [2026-10-21] Per the Economic Observer, the campus's source-grid-load-storage project was connected to the grid in Jul 2025. The 300 MW wind, solar and storage plant links to the campus by a 220 kV dedicated line. [2026-10-22] Per the Aug 2026 substation EIA, the data centre EIA was approved by the Ulanqab ecology bureau on 31 Jan 2023 (乌环察审[2023]1号). A major change was re-approved on 22 Apr 2025 (乌环察审[2025]9号) to add operating equipment and raise rack power, with more standby diesel generators. Environmental acceptance work started in May 2025. The approved build is 20 compute buildings, 20 power buildings and 1 technical building. The site selection letter is dated 29 Jun 2022 and the land use planning permit 9 Aug 2024. The site is in the Bayin industrial park of the Chahar high-tech zone. [2026-10-22] The June 2024 substation EIA describes the base as 468,860 sqm of total floor area with 25,000 racks planned and a load scale of 338 MW (负荷规模33.8万千瓦). That is electrical load, not IT load. At the time about 200,000 sqm was under construction, of which 100,000 sqm had topped out. [2026-10-22] A related project, 京蒙绿色算力产业园二期, is being built by a separate company, 中金(乌兰察布)数据科技有限公司, in the same Bayin industrial park. Its EIA was approved by the Ulanqab ecology bureau on 26 Mar 2025 (乌环察审〔2025〕6号). It covers 250,296 sqm of land, 6 compute buildings plus 1 standby (D10), 12 power buildings plus 1 standby, about 13,500 racks and 8.4 billion yuan of investment, and was under construction by the time of the 2025 substation EIA. Its own 220/10kV substation has 4 x 240 MVA, with 5 planned 220kV circuits to Shengjiaying, CICC phase 1 (中金一期), Manda and two to renewables. Ulanqab approval 乌行审政服批字[2025]143号. Whether this is the Zone D expansion of this row is not stated. Owner review needed before attaching it. [2026-10-22] Science and Technology Daily (via Xinhua, 19 Oct 2026) says the base self-consumes about 848 GWh of green power a year from its directly connected 300 MW wind and solar plus 45 MW storage project, cutting about 580,000 tonnes of carbon. [2026-10-22] The campus 110kV substation is fed by two new 110kV bays at the Shengjiaying 220kV substation in Jining district (3 x 180 MVA) over a new 2 x 6.1 km double-circuit line, 2 x 5 km overhead and 2 x 1.1 km cable. Investment 28.30 million yuan, Ulanqab DRC approval 乌发改批字[2024]39号, works planned for Aug to Oct 2024. [2026-10-23] China Economic Net (22 Oct 2026) gives the zero-carbon computing base (574 mu) as 360 MW of planned capacity, in operation since Aug 2024. It lists the Jing-Meng data economy park (530 mu, 1,035 MW), the green intelligent computing base (430 mu, 480 MW) and a 501 mu plot about 7 km north (840 MW), for over 2.7 GW across 2,035 mu. These are press figures, not filings, so planned MW is not set. The Aug 2024 start conflicts with the held Jul 2025 operational date. [2026-10-23] China Energy Engineering's North China institute won the EPC for a 380 MW source-grid-load-storage project (280 MW wind, 100 MW solar, 57.5 MW / 230 MWh storage and a new 220kV booster substation) in Chahar Right Front Banner, on 30 Sep 2025 (CEEC release of 18 Oct 2025). The client is 中金（察哈尔右翼前旗）新能源科技有限公司. It is phase 2 of the green power base for 中金数据's Ulanqab zero-carbon computing park. It is not yet tied to a zone of this row.

facilities.notes: The data centre opened in 2020, and its three self-built rooms were full by 2023 (Beijing News). [2026-10-22] Beijing News (1 Sep 2026) quotes an Alibaba Ulanqab staff member: the data centre was completed and put into operation in 2020, and its three self-built facilities filled up after the 2023 AI wave. facilities.notes: The first center cost 447 million yuan and was built in about 16 months. It entered full production in October 2023. Intelligent computing phase 1 started in October 2024 in Xifeng. It was topped out in about a year and in January 2026 was preparing for commissioning, with 272 high-power racks due first. In September 2026 Xinhua Finance reported one building operating and fully leased to a single large client (unnamed), with three more buildings under construction. The 135MW figure is stated as compute or rack power capacity, not as IT load, so it is tagged total_power. Investment is unconfirmed. China Telecom planned 478 million yuan for 2024, and a 3.37 billion yuan phase 1 figure appears only in a directory headline that could not be opened. The 5GW green power figure in some coverage is supply potential, not site capacity. [2026-10-17] Xinhua Finance, 2026-09-10: three buildings under construction this year. A steel-frame building is moving to its third floor. One building is operating and fully leased to a major client (unnamed). (新华财经, 2026-09-10) [2026-10-17] China Telecom dates the intelligent computing centre groundbreaking to 23 Oct 2024. (澎湃号 中国电信集团有限公司官方账号, 2024-10-24) [2026-10-17] China Telecom gives the intelligent computing centre about 3.37bn yuan total investment, 182,840 sqm, 7 data centre buildings, 22,500 physical racks and 135MW of rack capacity. Phase 1 is 478 million yuan with 2,376 rack positions. The earlier 447 million yuan centre went live at end August 2023 and its 1,664 racks were sold out by end September 2024. (澎湃号 中国电信集团有限公司官方账号, 2024-10-24) [2026-10-18] China Telecom launched phase 2 of its Qingyang AI computing park on 18 May 2026: 3 data centre buildings and a 110kV substation. Kingsoft Cloud lit a high-performance cluster at the same ceremony, but the article does not say the cluster sits in China Telecom's park. (甘肃日报 (陇东报), 2026-05-19) [2026-10-19] In Aug 2026 China Telecom issued tenders for Qingyang intelligent computing centre related projects with combined budgets above 200 million yuan. Packages and winners were not itemised. [2026-10-23] Phase 3 civil EPC was tendered on 11 Aug 2026 in two lots for data centre buildings 6 and 7. Each building is 23,298 sqm with 1,675 IT rack positions, 1,602 of them powered, about 27.8MW and PUE no higher than 1.20. Planned works start 15 Sep 2026. The project filing is 庆市发改备〔2022〕9号. This is a tender, not an award. Planned MW is unchanged. [2026-10-23] The operations centre civil EPC (about 4,923.88 sqm on about 2.8 mu) was tendered on 27 Aug 2026 with a cap of 18.72 million yuan and a planned start of 1 Oct 2026. This is a tender, not an award.

facilities.notes: China Energy Engineering's own filing (10 Sep 2026) gives about 5.5 billion yuan total, of which about 2.25 billion is data center infrastructure and 1.21 billion is supporting renewables (150MW wind and 50MW solar). It gives about 60MW total power. Science and Technology Daily calls the 60MW design total IT power. A1 topped out on 22 Dec 2023, has operated since September 2024 and is above 99% occupied. A2 entered service in May 2026. A4 structure is complete and due by end 2026. A3 is due in 2027 after a liquid-cooling redesign. One June 2025 local report said only A1's main works were complete, which conflicts with the September 2024 operation date. The company filing is preferred. China Power Engineering Consulting Group, a CEEC unit, runs the integration and its Guangdong branch is the general contractor. The project was part of the 2023 private placement and received national policy-based development financing. A1 has been live since September 2024 and A2 went live in June 2026. A4 is due by end 2026 and A3 by June 2027. [2026-10-20] CEEC says the park is supplied over a virtual private line (虚拟专线供电) and has signed a long-term green power contract (绿电长协). Power costs are about 45 percent of revenue and depreciation about 40 percent. The live part is over 85 percent racked, mainly by leading internet companies. A4 is in M&E installation and has a memorandum of cooperation with a customer. The customer is not named. [2026-10-21] Science and Technology Daily (11 Jun 2026) says racks are rated 12 to 140 kW and A1 is over 99 percent racked. It says A4 has finished construction and should operate by end 2026, and A3 by end June 2027. This is earlier than the held CEEC note that A4 is in M&E installation. [2026-10-22] The 110kV Nengjian No.1 substation, built under EPC by CEEC Guangdong Institute, was energised on 4 Sep 2024. It is the first substation in the Qingyang big data industrial park. [2026-10-23] MW and rack conflict: a March 2026 piece sourced to the Qingyang finance bureau gives total IT power of 70MW (IT总功率7万千瓦) and about 24,000 planned standard racks, of which about 8,000 are 8 to 12kW high-density racks able to reach 25kW. The row holds 60MW and 7,000 racks from the company filing. The campus is 110 mu with 87,000 sqm of floor area. Operator entity is 中能建绿色数字科技（庆阳）有限公司.

Cooling uses magnetic levitation chillers with an added cooling tower. [2026-10-20] By Jun 2023 phase 3 civil works were complete. Phase 3 cost about 0.9 billion yuan and covers two machine buildings and two power centres, adding over 7,000 racks. The full campus is to exceed 20,000 racks. China Mobile's Guiyang data centre is this Gui'an campus, so the link is ours. If 90MW is phase 4 alone, the campus total is above the held 90MW. Process load is not stated as IT load. No winner yet.

The source does not name the building, so the link to this row rests on China Telecom's Shaoguan hub being this campus. At the June 2026 conference phase 2 was under construction and phase 3 was about to start. [2026-10-17] As of 2026-06-12, China Telecom phase 2 was under construction. Phase 3 and the Shaotang site were about to start. China Mobile phase 2 and China Unicom phase 2 were also about to start. (科技日报, 2026-06-13) [2026-10-20] In Aug 2026 China Telecom tendered electromechanical works for the A7 intelligent computing centre at its Zhenjiang park in Shaoguan, together with the Shaotang phase 1.1 EPC. The Greater Bay Area tenders that month had a combined budget of over 2.7 billion yuan. The A7 budget and winner are not stated. [2026-10-21] The Guangdong DRC energy review (reported Apr 2023) covers 5,132 racks of 6 kW and 1,723 racks of 8 kW, equal to 17,830 standard racks, with annual electricity capped at 335.15 GWh and PUE not above 1.2472. This is below the 50,400 racks held, so it likely covers the first phase only. [2026-10-22] China Telecom tendered the phase 2.2 EPC for the A3 and A4 intelligent computing centres at the Zhenjiang park on 7 Aug 2026. The package covers two buildings of about 36,540 sqm each, about 73,100 sqm in total, plus outdoor generator platforms, on a 26,615 sqm plot (ZC0201A-10-2). Total investment is 404.06 million yuan ex-tax and the planned duration is 297 calendar days. No winner was read. [2026-10-23] Approval: the Guangdong energy bureau approved the phase II energy review on 26 Jan 2025 (粤能许可〔2025〕11号) for China Telecom Guangdong. Phase II has 3 data centres, 3 intelligent computing centres and 3 power centres, with 8,286 racks, equal to 58,253 standard racks. Annual electricity is capped at 1,433.29 GWh and PUE at 1.249. Listed equipment includes chillers and air conditioning. With the 17,830 standard racks of phase I, the reviewed total is above the 50,400 racks held.

facilities.notes: Construction started on 24 Nov 2023 with a plan for 10,000 racks. Later official figures give 8,750 racks at full build. Phase 1 is operating and Phase 2 is due by end 2026. The Wuhu government cites 120MW total power. That is not IT load. A Phase 2 entry appeared on the Anhui key project list in Sep 2026. [2026-10-18] Phase 1 civil works topped out on 30 May 2024 and MEP works began the same day. The full plan is 4 data centre buildings, 2 operations buildings, a 110kV substation and 2 generator platforms, about 87,700 sqm in total. (芜湖市人民政府, 2024-06-03) [2026-10-20] The Wuhu ecology and environment bureau approved the EIA for the 110kV substation on 11 Sep 2025 (芜辐射环审〔2025〕13号). The substation is in the south-west corner of the park at Wuyue Road and Dalongwan E2 Road, Jiangbei New Area. It is indoor, with four 63MVA transformers (two duty, two standby), built in one go with no later expansion. It has two 110kV incoming bays, one from Jiangbei and one from Jiaoji, and 36 10kV feeders. [2026-10-20] Phase 1 consists of one data centre building, one diesel generator platform building and one operations building. The full build targets 8,750 racks and 50,000P of compute. [2026-10-22] The builder's release says the site is about 96 mu (about 64,000 sqm) north of Dalongwan E2 Road, west of Wuyue Road and east of the Yunhu waterway in Jiangbei New Area. Total investment is 6 billion yuan and planned floor area is 90,400 sqm. It plans at least 10,000 racks averaging 6 kW, built to class A and Unicom T3+ standards. The 10,000 rack figure is above the 8,750 racks held, so it is noted, not changed. [2026-10-22] Phase 1 of the China Unicom YRD (Wuhu) intelligent computing centre passed completion acceptance filing on 26 Nov 2025: data centre building A (16,270.09 sqm, 5 storeys), operations building A (3,586.6 sqm), generator platform A (1,929.78 sqm) and the gatehouse. The owner is 中国联合网络通信有限公司芜湖市分公司.

A UPS supplier release in Mar 2026 cited over 7,800 racks. A separate China Mobile YRD (Wuhu) second data centre is on the Anhui key project list (Sep 2026) with no figures yet. A separate China Mobile YRD (Wuhu) Second Data Centre EIA was returned at the applicant's request on 2026-08-21. It is held as a distinct lead until its scale is published. [2026-10-17] Total investment is about 6bn yuan, built to national Grade A standard. Planned compute is up to 22 EFLOPS, which is compute and not IT load. (中华网 (from 看点时报), 2026-03-20) [2026-10-19] China.com Tech (2026-03-20) reports EAST Group (易事特) supplied the UPS system. Equipment supply, so not listed as a contractor. [2026-10-20] Phase 2 works started, reported 2025-04-23 (DTDATA via Sina Finance). Phase 2 is about 33,000 sqm with a 110kV substation. The row's construction start stays 2024-10-17. [2026-10-20] Phase 2 works started, reported on 2025-04-23. The same report says IT load can reach 101MW. This is press, not a filing, so planned MW stays blank. Planned racks are 1,278 AI racks at 40kW and 6,537 general racks at 7kW. Liquid cooling is listed among the technologies used, without detail. Land is about 96.5 mu, matching the held 64,327 sqm. facilities.notes: The design plan was published on 24 May 2024 on a 262,436 sqm plot with 347,671 sqm of floor area. The EIA was accepted in Jan 2025. Wuhu said in Jul 2026 that Douyin projects are live and that Douyin's continued construction is supported. That statement does not name this site, so the live date is unconfirmed. Stage held at land and permitting because no dated source ties construction or operation to this site. [2026-10-14] 2026-07-29 local report says Douyin's Wuhu computing project is built and operating (建成投运), with continued construction (续建) under way. The source says 抖音 and does not name 火山引擎 or 芜湖江东名邑科技, so stage not changed; treat as strong indication construction has begun and a first phase is live. (大江资讯（新京报新京号）, 2026-07-29) [2026-10-15] Jiemian places the project in the Wuhu Economic and Technological Development Zone (芜湖经开区) under the ByteDance entity 芜湖江东名邑科技有限公司, with 21,800 server cabinets plus 236 network cabinets, a 220kV substation and 8 billion yuan. The page date is not shown and the 2024-05-24 date is the pre-approval notice it cites. The 2026-10-15 09:08 run described this centre as being in Wuwei; the zone stated here is the development zone. [2026-10-22] The Anhui DRC approved the project energy report on 6 Nov 2024 (project code 2403-340264-04-01-358840). It gives 8 billion yuan of investment and about 393.5 mu of land. Phase 1 has three data centre buildings, three generator and water tank buildings, one complex building and one 220kV substation. No IT load was read. [2026-10-22] The site is two parcels sold by the Wuhu natural resources bureau (132,704 sqm and 129,732 sqm, together 262,436 sqm, matching the design plan notice). The single 262,436 sqm land entry was replaced by the two parcels so the area is not counted twice. [2026-10-22] Wuhu's housing bureau lists completion acceptance filings (竣工验收备案) by 芜湖江东名邑科技有限公司 for 火山引擎长三角算力中心项目A期: the 7-1 data centre (26,068 sqm, 2 storeys) and the 7-1 generator building on 27 May 2025, under construction permit 340207202411060201. The construction start is dated November 2024 from the permit number, which carries its issue date of 6 Nov 2024. No opening date was found, so the stage is held at under construction. [2026-10-22] The A phase 7-2 data centre (26,095.82 sqm, 2 storeys) and 7-2 generator building passed completion filing on 3 Jul 2025, and the A phase complex building (11,378.9 sqm, 13 storeys) on 10 Jul 2025. [2026-10-22] The A phase 220kV substation building (4,278.04 sqm) passed completion filing on 5 Aug 2025. [2026-10-22] The A phase 7-3 data centre (48,504.23 sqm, 4 storeys) and 7-3 generator building passed completion filing on 28 Sep 2025. [2026-10-22] The B phase 7-7 data centre (48,508.07 sqm, 4 storeys) and 7-7 generator building passed completion filing on 30 Oct 2025. So by end Oct 2025 four data centre buildings of about 149,000 sqm had been completed across phases A and B. No operating date was found.

[2026-10-20] A 2017 trade report (机房360 via 中国IDC圈, 2017-08-10) gives an annual average PUE below 1.3 for Qingpu, with absorption chillers on recovered trigeneration heat and cooling-tower free cooling. The lowest monthly PUE was 1.25 and the hottest month stayed below 1.4. Trigeneration supplied 39 percent of the site's power. Maglev chillers were also in use. The site received a 5A rating under the national data centre green grade scheme (operations) in May 2017.

facilities.notes: Phase 2 stage 3 topped out in Nov 2022 and phase 3 stage 3 passed early completion acceptance by Feb 2023. China Construction First Group (中建一局) built three projects of about 185,800 sqm. Xinhua says phase 1 was fully completed and put into operation in Dec 2025 (month only). Hebei Daily gives 700 MW IT in operation and 18 billion yuan investment. The ND11 building is on the MIIT 2025 green data centre list. Planned site is about 1,000 mu. ByteDance is often linked to the park in secondary reports, but no source names a tenant. [2026-10-19] Hoyinn was named a national computing and power synergy (算电协同) demonstration case. [2026-10-20] Xinhua (9 Apr 2026) says phase 1 took five years to build and has over 200,000 servers deployed. Some of its projects run on 100 percent green power, and energy storage is used to shift compute work when wind and solar output varies. [2026-10-20] SPD Bank Beijing branch provided financing in 2023 for the second stage of phase 1 construction. Loan size is not stated. [2026-10-21] Phase 2 stage 3 is a waste heat recovery heating pilot. With other pilots it heats about 200,000 sqm of floor space. [2026-10-21] In Mar 2026 豫能控股 (001896.SZ) agreed to put 1.1 billion yuan into 先天算力, a Henan Investment Group unit that plans to buy 91.2 percent of 郑州合盈 for 9.412 billion yuan. 郑州合盈 holds Hoyinn's data centres in Huailai and Langfang, including this park. As of 28 Feb 2026 it had delivered about 579 MW of IT to customers, with about 683 MW more planned. The 579 MW covers Huailai and Langfang together and is below the 700 MW held for this park, so it is a platform figure, not a change.

[2026-10-14] The 2026-09-21 filing funds phase two (2# data hall, 3# admin building, external mains power works, landscaping) with RMB 787.0118 million; phase one covers the 1# data hall and supporting works. No contractor, PUE or substation disclosed. (首都在线（SZ300846）公告, 2026-09-21) Phase 1 passed acceptance in mid 2026 and its high-power racks are leased to an unnamed leading internet company. [2026-10-16] Shanghai Securities News (2026-10-12) says phase 1 was completed and accepted in mid 2026 and the project has moved into operation, so the stage is now operational, dated to that report. Phase 2 (about 40MW) is still to be built. The tenant is an unnamed leading internet company, so no client is added. [2026-10-17] Phase 2 of the computing centre has a planned total investment of 787.01m yuan, all funded from the 2026 A-share placement. It covers machine room building 2, integrated building 3 and the external power works, on 18,926.49 sqm of company-owned land in Huailai. Racks are 12kW and can be upgraded to 24kW. Phase 1 is building 1. Phase 1 cost about 319m yuan. (Beijing Capital Online (SZSE 300846), 2026-09-21) [2026-10-19] The revised feasibility report (2026-09-21) says phase 2 will provide 40MW of high-power server rack supply (40MW 高功率低功耗服务器机柜资源的供应能力). Phase 1 MW is not stated, so planned MW stays blank. [2026-10-19] The 2026-09-21 feasibility report lists external utility power works (外市电工程) in phase 2 scope but gives no substation voltage, MVA, PUE or cooling method. Racks are 12kW and can be upgraded to 24kW. [2026-10-21] Phase 1 (building 1, 10MW) reached ready-for-use status on 30 Jun 2026 after completion acceptance and entered operation in July 2026. This is earlier than the held operational date of 12 Oct 2026. In July 2026 the whole 10MW was leased to an unnamed Customer A for one year, on discounted terms. For phase 2 (40MW) the company holds letters of intent for about 52MW. The operating company is 怀来智慧云港科技有限公司. [2026-10-21] Approvals listed by the company: energy review 冀发改环资〔2023〕1175号 (15 Sep 2023). Phase 2 EIA filing 怀行审建环备字〔2026〕1号 (18 Mar 2026). Phase 2 project filing 怀行审建备字〔2026〕39号 (28 Feb 2026). Land title 冀（2022）怀来县不动产权第0021494号 (8 Sep 2022). Land use planning permit 地字第130730202200056号 (30 Aug 2022). Works planning permit 建字第130730202500029号 (11 Jun 2025). At 21 Oct 2026 phase 2 had not started and had no construction permit. [2026-10-21] The Q3 2026 report says construction in progress fell 72 percent from end 2025 because the Jingbei project was completed and moved to fixed assets. On 20 Oct 2026 the board proposed up to 815 million yuan of new guarantees for bank credit to 怀来智慧云港, to fund construction of the computing centre. [2026-10-22] CapitalOnline's revised placement feasibility report (21 Sep 2026) plans 787.0118 million yuan for 京北云计算软件研发中心项目-算力中心（二期）. Phase 2 covers the 2# machine room, the 3# comprehensive building, external mains power, roads and greening. On completion it is to supply 40MW of high-power server rack capacity, using 12kW racks that can be raised to 24kW. Phase 1 was the 1# machine room. The 40MW is a phase 2 figure against the 50MW held, so it is noted, not changed. No start date is given. [2026-10-22] CapitalOnline's revised reply to the SZSE inquiry (21 Oct 2026) says AIDC phase 1 at Huailai, the 1# machine building of about 10MW, reached ready-for-use state in June 2026 after completion acceptance and was moved to fixed assets that month. Spending began in 2023. Construction in progress was 91.41 million yuan at end 2025 and 340.90 million yuan was transferred in H1 2026. The June 2026 completion is earlier than the held under_construction entry of 2026-09-21.

facilities.notes: Phase 1 was built in 2013. Three data buildings were live with 10,800 racks in Aug 2024. DC4 and DC5 passed initial acceptance on 15 Aug 2025. DC6 to DC8 broke ground on 19 Jun 2025 with about 150,000 sqm of floor space. The full plan has 16 data buildings and is described as gigawatt-class, but no IT MW is stated. The site already hosts the three telcos, financial firms and large internet customers, none named. [2026-10-14] Dated stage moves: DC6, DC7 and DC8 broke ground on 2025-06-19, and DC4/DC5 passed initial acceptance on 2025-08-15 (C114, 2025-10-13). China Unicom Inner Mongolia tendered DC14 and DC17 civil EPC (about 38,200 sqm each, total investment CNY 548.18m) on 2026-08-27 (C114, 2026-08-31), with no award found yet. Contractors are still empty. (C114通信网, 2025-10-13) [2026-10-18] Trade press gives an IT capacity target of 60MW for the DC6 building alone. It is a single-building figure, so planned MW for the campus stays blank. China Unicom's DC6, DC7 and DC8 electromechanical works at Hohhot totalled about 2.045 billion yuan ex-tax in H1 2026 awards. (通信产业报 (网易号), 2026-07-14) [2026-10-19] In August 2026 China Unicom tendered new-build civil works for DC11 and DC12 at the Hohhot base, budget 627 million yuan, and a No. 3 220kV substation in Hohhot, budget 249 million yuan. No winners were named. [2026-10-19] In September 2026 China Unicom tendered four EPC lots for DC17 and DC14 new-build phase 1 at the Hohhot Cloud Data Base, covering base electromechanical and customer support works. Lot budgets were 298, 290, 286 and 276 million yuan, about 1.15 billion yuan in total. No winners were named. [2026-10-20] On 27 Aug 2026 China Unicom Inner Mongolia tendered the DC14 and DC17 civil new-build works in the Hongsheng industrial park, with planned investment of 548.18 million yuan. Each building is about 38,200 sqm, four storeys and 31.95m high. The EPC lots were estimated at 270.77 and 273.48 million yuan, with a 130 day build period. No winners were named. [2026-10-20] C114 says the Hohhot base is planned at a scale of about a thousand mu and a gigawatt (千亩、千兆瓦级). This is not stated as IT load, so planned MW stays blank. [2026-10-20] A bid shortlist dated 16 Oct 2026 ranks two consortia first for the DC17 and DC14 electromechanical phase 1 (customer support) EPC lots. DC17: 中讯邮电咨询设计院 (lead) with 华为技术服务 and 中建一局集团建设发展, bid 276 million yuan ex-tax. DC14: 北京电信规划设计院 (lead) with 深圳市中兴通讯技术服务, bid about 270 million yuan ex-tax. These are first-ranked candidates, not final awards. [2026-10-21] The DC17 and DC14 electromechanical phase 1 works were tendered in September 2026 as four EPC lots, covering base electromechanical works and customer support works. Lot budgets were 298, 290, 286 and 276 million yuan, about 1.15 billion yuan in total. No winners are named in this source. [2026-10-22] China Daily (Sep 2016) says construction of the China Unicom Northwest (Hohhot) base began on 1 Jul 2012, to be completed over ten years in three phases. It gives about 12.3 billion yuan of investment, 598,000 sqm of floor area and a service capacity of 33,000 racks and 560,000 servers. The 33,000 racks differ from the 30,000 held, so this is noted, not changed.

facilities.notes: The Zhangbei county media centre reported the groundbreaking on 10 August 2024: about 200 mu, 130MW planned total power capacity (计划总用电容量), nearly 12,000 racks. The company says phase 1 is 60MW with 59.35% of racks occupied at 30 June 2026; it does not say whether 60MW is IT load. Kaiyuan Securities (2026-08-25) says a 60MW phase 2 was contracted in January 2026 for delivery in the second half of 2026 and a 48MW phase 3 intent order is locked. The phases add to 168MW, above the 130MW total power in the 2024 plan. Planned MW is blank because no IT load is stated. [2026-10-15] The company said phase 1 passed completion acceptance and entered use at the end of October 2025. (和讯网 (腾讯新闻), 2026-04-22) [2026-10-15] Dawei signed a framework agreement on 2024-11-30 with an unnamed internet company for the custom phase 1, for about 10 years. (和讯网 (腾讯新闻), 2026-04-22) [2026-10-17] The project was first filed in August 2016 and stalled during the company debt crisis. Building restarted in 2024. Cumulative spend was 601 million yuan by May 2025, mostly to Beijing Changkong Construction and the grid works contractor. (大位数据科技（广东）集团股份有限公司 (SSE filing 2025-044), 2025-05-10) [2026-10-18] TMTPost gives the general contract for the project as 3,070 million yuan, on 200 mu with four data centre buildings. It also says a 145kV power station is built alongside, while the company filing describes a 110kV supply line. The 145kV figure is likely an error and is not stored. (钛媒体APP (腾讯新闻), 2025-03-20) [2026-10-19] The 2026-02-10 exchange announcement says phase 1 was completed and handed over in October 2025, earlier than the 2026-06-30 date held. Owner to confirm which date marks opening. [2026-10-19] Stage date conflict: in a stock exchange announcement on 2026-02-10 the company said phase 1 of the Zhangbei data centre was completed and handed over in October 2025. A broker note (KY Securities, 2026-05-28) says phase 1 passed completion acceptance at the end of October 2025 and was put into use. The held operational date of 2026-06-30 is later. [2026-10-19] KY Securities (2026-08-25), citing the 2026 half-year report, says a phase 2 business contract of 60MW was signed in January 2026 for delivery in the second half of 2026. A further 48MW phase 3 order is agreed in principle but not yet a formal contract. Phase 1 rack fill (上架率) was 59.35% at 30 June 2026. The 60MW and 48MW are contract figures, not a stated IT load, so planned MW is not changed. [2026-10-20] The 2026 half-year report says phase 1 (60MW) passed completion acceptance and was delivered in two batches, on 30 Sep 2025 and 30 Oct 2025. The customer framework agreement was signed on 30 Nov 2024. After a 45-day free commissioning period, billing began in November 2025. This supports an operational date in late 2025, earlier than the held 2026-06-30. Owner check. [2026-10-20] Planned capacity across phases 1 to 3 is 168MW (60MW, 60MW and 48MW), all for one internet customer that is not named. Phase 2 deliveries began in July 2026, with full delivery due in H2 2026. These are contract figures, not a stated IT load, so planned MW is not changed. [2026-10-20] Changkong Construction won the main works by public tender in December 2024. Its scope is MEP for DC building 1, civil and MEP for DC buildings 2 and 3, civil works for DC building 4, and site utilities. In 2026 the contract was changed so the owner buys the core MEP equipment itself. The rest of building 2 and building 3 are due in 2026 and building 4 in 2027. By 30 Jun 2026 Changkong had finished building 1 MEP, civil works for buildings 2 and 3, and part of their MEP. [2026-10-20] Financing: from March to July 2026 the Zhangbei unit signed finance leases with 交银金融租赁 for phase 2 MEP and IDC equipment, with 1,045.28 million yuan principal. On 24 Jun 2026 it signed a 1.202 billion yuan syndicated fixed-asset loan with Industrial Bank and SPDB for phases 1 and 2. [2026-10-22] A Jiemian summary of a Feb 2026 Dawei trading announcement says the first stage of the Zhangbei data centre was finished and delivered in Oct 2025 and contributed little 2025 revenue. That is earlier than the held operational date of 30 Jun 2026. Owner check. The date shown is the announcement week.

facilities.notes: Ya'an is a named site of the Tianfu computing cluster. This row is the whole park, not one building. The park reports 45,000 standard racks delivered and a target of 60,000 by end-2026. Alibaba and ByteDance are reported as tenants at park level only. Chuanxi Data is the largest operator, with nearly 7,000 racks, and China Construction Bank lent it working capital in Q1 2026. No MW or investment figure is published. The Alibaba Western Cloud row is in Chengdu and does not count Ya'an. The park's exact location is not given, so coordinates are at city level. [2026-10-16] Big-data power in Ya'an costs as little as 0.34 yuan per kWh on local hydropower. (封面新闻, 2026-09-01) [2026-10-19] Trade press says the park has about 45,000 racks and 9,431P of compute, of which over 8,558P is intelligent compute. The park's annual PUE is 控制在1.25以下, helped by a 15.6C average temperature. This is an operating figure, not a design PUE, and no cooling method is named. [2026-10-19] On 21 May 2024 Ya'an signed three AI projects described as upgrading the park. They were a 7.5 billion yuan AI computing project with 中建三局 planning 1,700 high power racks and a substation, the 7 billion yuan 善思云 centre, and a Baidu 1024P centre of at least 0.5 billion yuan. These are separate projects and are not added to this row. [2026-10-19] China Mobile's Ya'an branch has been in the park since early 2020 and has invested over 3 billion yuan. It runs buildings No. 2 and No. 4 on its own, with over 4,000 racks in operation, making it the largest carrier in the park. [2026-10-19] A Chuanxi Data deputy general manager said in April 2026 that the company holds nearly 7,000 racks. The rest of the park's about 45,000 racks are run by other operators, so the operator figure is much smaller than the park figure.

facilities.notes: A Guohai Securities note (2026-10-12) says that by the 2026 interim report the Ulanqab 496.8MW green intelligent computing centre had approval from the Ulanqab Development and Reform Commission, with preliminary procedures, power supply and financing in progress. The stage date is the end of August 2026, when interim reports are due, because the approval date is not given. The 496.8MW has no stated basis (IT load or power capacity), so planned MW is blank. Jinkai signed with Ulanqab on 10 Feb 2026 alongside China Unicom, Boda Data and one other firm; those four projects total about 1,600MW of IT load and about 285,000 racks combined, with no split by project. The district is not published, so coordinates are at city level. [2026-10-17] The approval named in the H1 2026 report is a two-high (high energy use, high emissions) project assessment opinion. Ulanqab DRC issued it jointly with three other departments under document 乌发改环资字〔2026〕392号. It is not a project filing. At the 2026-09-23 results briefing the company said pre-construction procedures, technical plan, power supply and financing were still in progress. It gave no start date and would not say whether the project has customers. No investment, IT load, racks or district were disclosed. (Stockstar (company announcement), 2026-09-23) [2026-10-23] Jinkai New Energy said on 18 Sep 2026 that phase 1 of its Ulanqab green computing build, a 124MW computing project, has been filed (已备案) and is expected in operation in 2027. The company does not say whether 124MW is IT load, so planned MW stays blank. This is a project filing, separate from the two-high assessment opinion already held.
